questions.note: Order reads right: hallux longest, toe 2 shorter, the hallux now about 24 mm deep at the IP with a round pulp, toe 2 with a PIP knuckle. But both joints wear one stamp of long parallel grooves that notch the profile, toe 2's DIP crease is a knife cut with ~8 mm of bare skin before its nail, the web ends in a shelf, and from below the hallux is a straight bar and toe 2 shows a seam.

Both nails sit right, with a fold and a thick free edge trimmed straight; nothing floats or sinks. But they read as press-on acrylic: a uniform pale-pink tile with a thin bright rim along the sides, a constant-width opaque cream tip on both (a French manicure), squared slab corners, an acrylic sheen, and no visible lunula on the hallux.

Absent. The first MTP dorsum and the hallux's proximal phalanx are a smooth dome in the front, medial and clay views: no EHL cord, no extensor slip to toe 2. A lean 40-year-old's forefoot shows the EHL as a soft ridge catching the light, as the anchor photos do.

SSS holds: the toes' shadow sides stay dark and nothing glows. The micro-relief is there but reads wrong: a crumpled-cellophane crackle that glitters in highlights and is alike on knuckle, shaft and web, a blank pulp under the nail, and plantar ridges as straight diagonal stripes. Broad glossy highlights on the dorsum read as polished silicone (skin materials are a declared first pass).

defects.what: The hallux nail reads as a press-on tile: a uniform pale-pink rounded rectangle in an even gutter, with a thin bright rim along both side margins, so every edge shows.
defects.fix: Let the lateral folds roll over the plate's edges so it disappears under skin, and give the plate faint longitudinal ridges and a tone that shifts from root to free edge.

defects.what: Both free edges are a constant-width opaque cream band (a crisp white line on toe 2), which reads as a French manicure tip.
defects.fix: A trimmed free edge varies a little in width, is translucent whitish-yellow so the hyponychium tints it, and carries a faint grime line underneath.

defects.what: No EHL tendon: the first MTP dorsum and the hallux's proximal phalanx are one smooth dome, toe 2 has no extensor slip, and the medial profile from instep to hallux is a clean curve with no cord.
defects.fix: Raise the EHL as a 4–5 mm cord, 0.5–1.5 mm proud, over the first MTP and along the hallux's proximal phalanx, fading at the IP, and a fainter extensor slip onto toe 2, both catching the rim light.

defects.what: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wear the same stamp: 3–4 long, evenly spaced, parallel glossy grooves spanning the joint, which notch the silhouette like bellows in the medial view.
defects.fix: Knuckle skin shows a cluster of short, broken, uneven creases of varying depth, a few deeper ones curving round a slightly darker, looser pad; vary them per toe and keep them out of the silhouette.

defects.what: The plantar ridges are straight parallel stripes at one diagonal angle over the ball, both pads and the phalanges, crossing the creases; at native size the underside reads as corduroy or brushed metal.
defects.fix: Friction ridges follow the surface: whorls or loops on the pads, arcs on the ball, running round the toe sides and breaking at flexion creases, too fine to read as stripes at native size.

defects.what: The 1–2 web ends in a straight lip: a flat shelf of skin between the hallux and toe 2 that drops into a dark slot (also in the front view and in clay).
defects.fix: A web margin is a soft U, deepest midway, with the dorsal skin curving down into the cleft and rising along each toe's side.

defects.what: From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball along a straight medial line with no toe-base crease, and its sides stay nearly parallel to the tip, so it reads as a rounded bar.
defects.fix: Give a deep curved toe-base crease between ball and toe, a narrower neck at the IP crease, and an oval pulp dome visibly wider than the neck.

defects.what: Toe 2's distal segment reads finger-long: about 8 mm of bare skin between the DIP crease and the proximal nail fold, so the nail sits at the very end of a long tip.
defects.fix: On a second toe the nail fold starts 3–4 mm past the dorsal DIP crease; move the crease distally or the nail proximally so the plate covers most of the distal segment.

defects.what: From below a thin pale seam rings toe 2 at mid-length with a step in its outline, so the toe's end reads as a cap fitted on, like the old toes 3–4.
defects.fix: Blend the tip into the shaft; at the PIP use a soft, dark flexion fold that does not stand as a raised ring.

defects.what: A thin raised glossy arc crosses the first MTP dorsum and nicks the medial profile (two notches in the medial view); it reads as a healed surgical scar.
defects.fix: At rest the skin over the first MTP shows a few faint, short, soft creases or none; remove the raised arc.

defects.what: The hallux tuft is about ten straight, uniformly dark strokes clustered into <, | and Λ shapes; at native size they read as pen scratches rather than hair.
defects.fix: Curve each hair slightly, taper it to a lighter brown tip, lay all distally with only 10–20° yaw, and spread them over the 12 × 10 mm patch.

defects.what: No lunula shows on the hallux: the proximal plate is the same pink as the rest apart from a specular blob.
defects.fix: A dull, slightly paler half-moon about 3.5 mm deep, centred, with a soft convex distal border, partly under the fold.

defects.what: Toe 2's DIP crease is one long, even groove with a bright lip across most of the toe: a knife cut.
defects.fix: Two or three short, soft, broken creases, shallower toward their ends.

defects.what: In the highlight the dorsal micro-relief breaks into sharp angular facets like crumpled cellophane, and the same crackle covers knuckle, shaft and web alike.
defects.fix: Skin relief is soft rounded plateaus between fine grooves, finer over knuckles and web, coarser on the shaft; highlights break into many small soft glints.

defects.what: The hallux free edge is an opaque grey-cream strip of constant width ending in squared, millimetre-thick slab corners resting on the skin.
defects.fix: Round the corners off into the lateral folds, make the edge translucent whitish so the pulp tints it, and let its width vary slightly along the trim.

defects.what: The visible plate is washed near-white by a broad soft highlight with soft vertical combing, like polished acrylic.
defects.fix: Keratin shows a smaller, softer sheen broken by fine longitudinal ridges and slight unevenness.

defects.what: Below the hallux free edge the hyponychium and pulp are blank and soft while the side wall beside them carries a crisp crackle.
defects.fix: Carry the fine skin relief and the pad's ridges onto the pulp, up to the hyponychium.

defects.what: The hallux nail's medial margin is an S-curve pinched in at mid-length, so the plate looks waisted (also in the material view).
defects.fix: The nail fold runs as a smooth, gently convex line and the plate is widest near the free edge.

defects.what: Toe 2 carries a single 1–2 mm hair stub, so it reads bald next to the hallux tuft.
defects.fix: Two to four hairs, 3–6 mm, lying distally on the proximal phalanx.

defects.what: From below toe 2's tip ends in a puckered, creased rim, as if the pulp were drawn in by a string.
defects.fix: The pad's end is a smooth rounded dome; at most the nail's free edge shows past it as a thin pale line.

defects.what: In clay a hairline crease runs down the junction of the web and toe 2's medial wall instead of a soft concave fillet.
defects.fix: Blend the web into the toe's side with a fillet of a few millimetres radius.

ranked: [D1] The hallux nail is a press-on: a uniform pale-pink tile in an even gutter with a thin bright rim along its sides; a real plate slides under rolled lateral folds and shifts in tone from root to edge.
[D2] Both free edges are a constant-width opaque cream band, a French manicure tip on a soldier's foot.

[D3] No extensor tendons: the first MTP and the hallux's proximal phalanx are a smooth dome and toe 2 has no extensor slip; a lean 40-year-old soldier's forefoot shows the EHL as a cord catching the light, as the anchor photos do.
[D4] The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wear one stamp of 3–4 long, parallel, glossy grooves that notch the profile like bellows; real knuckle creases are short, broken, uneven and differ from toe to toe.

[D5] The plantar ridges are straight diagonal stripes at one angle over ball, pads and phalanges, crossing the creases; at native size the underside reads as corduroy, not friction skin with whorls on the pads.
[D6] The 1–2 web ends in a straight shelf of skin over a dark slot, where a real web dips in a soft U between the toes.
[D7] From below the hallux is a straight-sided bar growing out of the ball with no toe-base crease and no neck, so it reads like a mannequin's thumb rather than a toe with an oval pad.
[D8] Toe 2's distal segment is finger-long: about 8 mm of bare skin between its DIP crease and its nail, which sits at the very tip.
[D9] From below a pale seam rings toe 2 at mid-length with a step in its outline, so the toe's end reads as a cap like the old toes 3–4.
[D10] A thin raised glossy arc across the first MTP dorsum nicks the medial profile and reads as a bunionectomy scar.
[D11] The hallux hair is about ten straight, equally dark strokes clustered into <, | and Λ shapes: pen scratches rather than fine, slightly curved hairs lying toward the tip.
[D12] No lunula shows on the hallux; most men's big toenails show a dull, paler half-moon at the root.
[D13] Toe 2's DIP crease is one long even groove with a bright lip, a knife cut rather than a few short soft creases.

Nothing shows wear for a boot-wearing 40-year-old: the nails have no ridging, thickening, yellowing or grime under the edge, and the hallux's medial IP has no pinch callus, so the toes read young and pampered.
[D14] The dorsal micro-relief glitters as crumpled cellophane in the highlights, one crackle on knuckle, shaft and web alike.
[D15] At the zoom the hallux free edge is an opaque grey strip ending in squared, millimetre-thick slab corners sitting on the skin.
[D16] The hallux plate's sheen is a broad near-white wash with soft vertical combing, like polished acrylic.
[D17] Under the hallux free edge the pulp is blank while the side wall beside it carries a crisp crackle: detail sharp in one place and soft in the next.
[D18] The hallux nail's medial margin is an S-curve pinched in at mid-length, so the plate looks waisted.
[D19] Toe 2 has a single 1–2 mm hair stub, nearly bald beside the hallux tuft.
[D20] From below toe 2's tip ends in a puckered, creased rim rather than a smooth pad dome.
[D21] In clay a hairline crease runs down the junction of the web and toe 2's medial wall instead of a soft fillet.
